venue.name: North Island Wildlife Recovery Centre
venue.description: The North Island Wildlife Recovery Centre at Errington is a non profit that cares for ill, injured and orphaned wildlife and educates the public about wildlife and environmental issues. More than sixty resident animals that cannot be released back to the wild live on the site, among them bald eagles, owls, black bears, hawks, turtles and ravens, and visitors walk gravelled paths between the enclosures. It is open every day from 9 am to 4.30 pm, closed only on Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day. School classes and community groups of 15 to 45 people can request either a volunteer guided tour or a self guided visit through a form on the site, but what a booked group pays is not published anywhere.
venue.address: 1240 Leffler Road, Box 364, Errington, BC V0R 1V0

facility_notes.washrooms: Washrooms are wheelchair accessible and have one baby changing station. They are located in the Eagle Flight Enclosure building.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Picnic areas with tables and benches are scattered around the grounds. Picnic tables are available for use after your tour for snack and/or lunch time.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Our paths are graveled and wheelchair accessible. Two wheelchairs are available for visitor use at no charge.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Bus parking is available (a parking map will be provided). Parking is free, and reserved spots for the disabled are in the main lot near the entrance.

restrictions: Cell phones are for photo use only. Please turn off flash and put phones in 'silent' mode while on-site
Any behaviour (such as running, yelling, rough-housing or playing tag) that frightens, causes stress or endangers the safety of our animals is unacceptable
Students must always stay with chaperones
Please note that free passes and Annual Memberships are not valid for booked tours
Please dress for the weather and be prepared to walk during the tour of the facility
venue.hours_notes: Open daily 9:00 am to 4:30 pm, seven days a week. Closed Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day.
venue.seasonal_notes: Open year round. School and group visit requests are processed on Mondays and Tuesdays, and the centre takes one group at a time, in either the morning or the afternoon. The centre says booking spots fill up quickly and recommends booking at least three weeks ahead.
venue.price_year_or_season: Admission was read from the live home page and visit page on 10 September 2026. No year or season is printed beside the figures.

programs.name: Volunteer guided school tour
programs.description: A volunteer guide walks a class around the centre for roughly 60 to 75 minutes, with the exact length depending on the age of the group, its interest and how much support the adults give. Requests go in through the school visit form and are processed on Mondays and Tuesdays. The centre takes one group at a time, in the morning or the afternoon, and recommends booking at least three weeks ahead because spots fill quickly. A volunteer guide is not guaranteed. If the group is more than 30 minutes late without calling, the guides leave and the visit becomes self guided. Groups are 15 to 45 students. What a school group pays is not published: after the request goes in the school tour coordinator sends a payment schedule, and payment is taken at the gift shop counter on arrival.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the gravelled paths from enclosure to enclosure behind a guide, stopping to look at eagles, owls, hawks, ravens, turtles and black bears and asking questions as they go. Afterwards they can sit at the picnic tables for a snack or lunch.
programs.our_note: It is sixty to seventy five minutes of walking outdoors with nowhere much to sit down, so have a plan for tired legs. You need one adult for every five children aged 12 and under, which is six grown ups for a class of thirty. Ask for the cost in writing when you send the request, because the figure only comes back with the payment schedule.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms with a change table are in the Eagle Flight Enclosure building, the paths are gravelled and take a wheelchair, and parking is free with room for a bus. Picnic tables are dotted around for lunch after the tour, but nothing is said about shelter if it rains.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission fees are waived for a support person/education aide(s) accompanying a student(s) with special needs; however, this person(s) does not count in the requested ratios.
programs.payment_timing: Payment is due upon arrival. Only the teacher in charge checks in at the gift shop to pay, by cash, debit or credit.
programs.cancellation_note: The centre is open rain or shine except in extreme weather, when a booking may be rescheduled. To cancel, or if you will be late on the day, call 250-248-8534 ext 3 and leave a message.

chaperone_ratio.applies_to: students ages 13 and older, where the site says one adult for every 10 to 15

programs.evidence: Guided tours are approximately 60–75 minutes and begin at the scheduled start time

programs.name: Self guided school visit
programs.description: The same school visit form lets a class come and go round the centre at its own pace with no volunteer guide. Groups are 15 to 45 students, requests are processed on Mondays and Tuesdays, and the centre takes one group at a time in the morning or the afternoon. A map of the grounds can be downloaded from the visit page. As with a guided tour, what a school group pays is not published and the coordinator sends a payment schedule after the request goes in.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the grounds at their own pace with the printed map, stopping at whichever enclosures they choose, and finishing at the picnic tables or the Field of Stones playground beside the wildlife garden.
programs.our_note: Without a guide there is nobody telling the children what they are looking at, so print the map first and share out the reading among the adults. The playground beside the wildlife garden is the place to let them run, because running near the animals is not allowed.
programs.practical_summary: Same grounds as the guided tour: gravelled paths that take a wheelchair, washrooms in the Eagle Flight Enclosure building, picnic tables and free parking with room for a bus. Nothing is said about cover if it rains.
programs.payment_timing: Payment is due upon arrival. Only the teacher in charge checks in at the gift shop to pay, by cash, debit or credit.
programs.cancellation_note: The centre is open rain or shine except in extreme weather, when a booking may be rescheduled. To cancel, or if you will be late on the day, call 250-248-8534 ext 3 and leave a message.

chaperone_ratio.applies_to: students ages 13 and older, where the site says one adult for every 10 to 15

programs.evidence: Enjoy and explore the Wildlife Recovery Centre at your own pace.

programs.name: Group visit for community and daycare groups
programs.description: Groups that are not schools, including daycares, organisations and teams, use a separate group visit form. It asks for the ages of the visiting children and offers the same choice of a volunteer guided tour of about 60 to 75 minutes or a self guided visit at your own pace. Groups are 15 to 45 people, one adult is needed for every 5 children aged 12 and under, and requests are processed on Mondays and Tuesdays. The centre asks that a large group does not go into the gift shop all at once because the space is limited. What a group pays is not published: the group tour coordinator sends a payment schedule after the request goes in, and payment is taken on arrival.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the gravelled paths between the enclosures to look at eagles, owls, bears and turtles, either behind a volunteer guide or on their own with the map, then eat at the picnic tables afterwards.
programs.our_note: This is the form to use if you are a daycare rather than a school. Fifteen is the smallest group they will take, so a small room may need to join up with another. One adult per five children under 13 is the rule, and the adults are charged admission as well.
programs.practical_summary: Gravelled paths that take a wheelchair, washrooms with a change table in the Eagle Flight Enclosure building, picnic tables for lunch and free parking with room for a bus. Rain cover and how long a self guided visit takes are not stated.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission fees are waived for a support person/aide(s) accompanying a person(s) with special needs; however, this support person(s) does not count in the requested ratios.
programs.payment_timing: Payment due upon arrival. Only the group leader checks in at the gift shop to pay, by cash, debit or credit.
programs.cancellation_note: The centre is open rain or shine except in extreme weather, when a booking may be rescheduled. To cancel, or if you will be late on the day, call 250-248-8534 ext 3 and leave a message.

chaperone_ratio.applies_to: children ages 13 and older, where the site says one adult for every 10 to 15

gaps: NO PRICE IS PUBLISHED FOR A BOOKED SCHOOL OR GROUP VISIT. Both trip planner PDFs say the tour coordinator sends a payment schedule after the request goes in. General admission on their own pages is $15 plus tax for an adult and $6 plus tax for children 4 to 16, with under 4s free, but nothing says a booked tour is charged at those rates, and free passes and annual memberships are explicitly not valid for booked tours. For a class of 30 children with 6 adults, the published admission rates would come to roughly $270 before tax. That figure is an inference from the general admission page, not a quote for a school group, so no cost has been recorded against any program here. Ask for the number in writing when you request your date.

No age or grade range is published for any of the visits. The school request form asks which grades are coming rather than setting a range, and the only age rules on the site are how many adults have to come with children of a given age. That is why the age fields are empty here.
Youngest age welcomed is not stated. Children 3 and under get in free, which is a price rather than a welcome age.
How long a self guided visit takes is not stated. Only the guided tour has a length, 60 to 75 minutes, and the single number recorded here is the top of that range so a schedule is not built short.

Whether there is anywhere indoors to shelter or eat if it rains is not stated. They say they are open rain or shine except in extreme weather, and ask you to dress for the weather and be prepared to walk, which suggests the visit is outdoors throughout.
Stroller access is not mentioned anywhere. The paths are described as gravelled and wheelchair accessible, which is not the same thing on gravel.
There is no minimum notice period. The centre recommends at least three weeks and says spots fill up quickly, but that is advice rather than a rule, so no lead time has been recorded.

Which days tours actually run is not published. The centre is open seven days a week and says requests are processed on Mondays and Tuesdays, which is about their office rather than about your visit date.
Every photograph on the site carries its file name in place of alt text, so the picture descriptions here were written after opening each image in a browser and looking at it.
The site is built on Wix but returns full page text to a plain fetch. Prices here were still re-read from the live page in a browser and matched.

conflicts.note: Their own two pages print admission slightly differently. The home page says $15 for an adult and $6 for a child aged 4 to 16 with tax on top, and the visit page shows the same figures with nothing said about tax. The numbers agree, so budget for tax being added and check the total when you pay.
